title: Can a small open code model write a cursor-stroke generator that fools a human-vs-bot detector?
lede: a 1.5B code model rewrites the cursor generator against the mimic-cursor detector: only 25 to 29% of its candidates run, and the reference detector stays at AUROC 1.000, tied with the component search at the same 24-candidate budget (one seed, preliminary negative).
summary: Replaces mimic-cursor's component search with Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B-Instruct, run on CPU, which reads the detector's score (and, in one condition, its feature gaps) and rewrites a Python stroke generator: 6 rounds of 4 candidates, the component search's per-round budget. Data, detector, reference detector and copy test are those of mimic-cursor (DUX, 46 people). The reference detector stays at AUROC 1.000 on held-out people in both conditions, as does the component search at 24 candidates (0.999 to 1.000, 8 runs). Only 7 of 24 (blind) and 6 of 24 (feedback) candidates were usable; the rest were rejected as banned tokens (likely imports), failed to load or crashed. Limitations: one seed per condition (three were planned), one small model, 24 candidates, no human templates available to the model, a sandbox whose import ban may account for some rejections. Preliminary and negative; a larger model on a GPU is an owner step.
